title: Detect a cycle
prompt: The connections in graph are one-way. Return true when the graph contains a cycle: a route that starts at some name and leads back to it. A name connected to itself is a cycle. The cycle may be in any part of the graph.
hints: In a diamond, where a points to b and c and both point to d, the search reaches d twice. Why is that not a cycle?
A cycle is found only when the search reaches a name that is still being explored, which means it is on the current path.
Keep a state for each name: visiting or done. Reaching a visiting name is a cycle. Reaching a done name is not. Start a search from every name not yet done.
checkLabels: a to b to c and back to a is a cycle.
A straight line has no cycle.
Two routes to the same name are not a cycle.
A name connected to itself is a cycle.
An empty graph has no cycle.
A cycle is found even when the first name is not part of it.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Treats any name reached a second time as a cycle.
Searches from the first name only and misses a cycle elsewhere.

feedback: Draw the diamond and trace your search. When it reaches the bottom name the second time, is that name still on the current path?
